human_intent: Keep improving the mobile-first life/calendar preview with very low friction, coherent time geometry, durable local-first habits, useful money projections and reusable event interactions, while making the product self-describing enough that future chats continue from contracts/current code instead of redesigning settled behavior.
already_decided: Canonical data ownership stays separate from views/projections.
The visible habit history has fourteen equal day columns ending at HOY.
Daily marks and trajectory points use the same fourteen X centers.
Trajectory is derived from behavior logs; it is not a second persisted truth.
Compressed whole-week free time is one passive full-width band; visible 30-minute empty slots remain interactive.
Dynamic content must remain reachable; one surface has one vertical scroll owner.
Unknown/blank habit semantics differ by tracker mode and positive Extras are never auto-failures.
A geometric X means an undesired event only.
The whole habit label rail toggles its graph; a tiny chevron is never the exclusive hit target.
Grid/time lines remain behind calendar events; event blocks keep breathing room from the grid.
Responsive behavior follows the actual container width, retains seven days and removes secondary detail before shrinking primary text into microtypography.
Universal event links use one top-right chain symbol; event-body click edits the link and chain click opens it; class editing remains reachable.
Opening an embedded calendar dialog must not move the outer page, recursively grow iframe height or create runaway scrolling.
Verified Habits IndexedDB cutover remains canonical; legacy localStorage is rollback evidence, not the owner.
Personal values/URLs/sensitive schedule data stay in their local/private owners, not public coordination.
high_value_targets: Reduce human actions/friction rather than add decorative information.
Keep Calendar, Habits and Money temporal geometry coherent.
Finish pending local-first export/import/snapshot and separate Calendar/Money migration work without undoing the Habits cutover.
Consolidate accumulated CSS/JS patches only through a controlled contract-preserving migration, not a rewrite.
Add functional and responsive visual regression gates so known failures do not reach the served page.
Use critique + implementation + repair in one LAB turn when possible.
known_failures: microtypography as the primary responsive strategy
multiple clickable cells for one compressed free-time band
outer-page scroll movement when a dialog opens
blind deletion of accumulated patches before canonical consolidation
asking the human to recover the inaccessible old chat

FAST.use_when: The requested change is explicit, local, reversible and does not require material architectural decisions.
forbidden_overhead: release receipts for ordinary LAB iteration

DEEP.use_when: The task is materially ambiguous, multi-file, design-heavy or benefits from deciding the space before editing.
sequence: CONTEXT FIRST: write the material understanding that can change execution
COMPLETE MAP: name all meaningful parts before diving into part one
DEVELOP: resolve important decisions under those headings
EXECUTE: implement as much of the map as tool/context boundaries allow
CRITIQUE: inspect the actual result for contradictions and lost value
REPAIR: fix worker-soluble failures in the same work cycle
DEEP.rule: Context/map/specification are decision compression, not deliverables to endlessly regenerate.

EXHAUSTIVE.use_when: The human explicitly requests exhaustive coverage/a numbered map, or the work is structural enough that omission risk dominates.
sequence: print the complete requested title map once
develop it at the requested depth
execute continuously from the frozen frontier
rules: A requested count such as 100 is a coverage matrix, not permission for filler.

A response-length boundary is not a project boundary; persist the frontier and continue.

CONTINUE.use_when: The conversation already has a materially sufficient context/map/specification or the human sends dot to continue.
